item.description: Plus: DoorDash to pay $131.5 million over minimum-pay law compliance and Trump weighs diesel export ban

item.title: Trump’s Oil Allies See Nightmare Scenario of Diesel-Export Ban Becoming Reality
item.description: American oil companies are fiercely opposed to the president’s nascent plan to ban exports of diesel, but vulnerable Republicans are putting pressure on him.

item.title: Swiss Parliament’s Upper House Backs Plan to Ease New Capital Demands on UBS
item.description: Under the proposal, the bank would be required to hold 90% in top-tier capital against its foreign subsidiaries, down from 100% the government previously planned.

item.title: Oil Prices Mixed as Traders Weigh U.S.-Iran Talks, Saudi Pipeline Progress
item.description: Saudi Arabia has begun testing its East-West pipeline for structural integrity and pressure, and American officials engaged in talks with Iranian peers on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

item.title: Dollar Jumps on U.S. Rate-Rise Bets
item.description: The dollar rose to an almost eight-week high against a basket of currencies, driven by expectations the Fed could raise interest rates further.

item.title: AI Cycle Set to Offset Energy Hit for Asia Economies
item.description: S&P raised its baseline projection for Asia’s 2026 gross domestic product growth to 4.6%, but noted that projections for strong growth this year and next don’t mask the challenges.

item.title: The Behind-the-Scenes Push to Get Xi a Red Carpet Welcome in America
item.description: The two sides have spent weeks discussing the trappings of the Chinese leader’s Washington visit, while leaving the biggest sources of tension largely untouched.

item.title: Japan’s Leader Calls on U.N. to Drop ‘Enemy State’ Label
item.description: China has used language in the United Nations charter to attack Japan as part of a broad pressure campaign that Tokyo wants Washington to help bring to an end.

item.title: Trump Threatens to Annihilate Iran as He Lays Out Foreign-Policy Vision at U.N.
item.description: President Trump labeled himself a man of peace while threatening to “annihilate” Iran and wield American power against other nations.

item.title: Zelensky Asks Trump for Winter Arms Package, Expects Energy-Ceasefire Push
item.description: In a WSJ interview, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia’s Putin is unlikely to curb attacks without more pressure from Washington.

item.title: Cocaine Smugglers Blow Past Europe’s Law Enforcement With Speedboats and Tech
item.description: Fleets outrun Spanish authorities to deliver the drug in unmatched quantity and quality.

item.title: World Leaders Almost All Agree on One Thing: The U.N. Is Failing
item.description: The spread of war has revived calls for the Security Council membership to expand beyond the U.S., Russia, China, France and the U.K.

item.title: Squeezed at Sea, Iran Faces New Restrictions on Its Flights
item.description: U.S. threats of secondary sanctions against airports see routes closed off for Iranian carriers.

item.title: Oil Prices Fall on U.S.-Iran Diplomacy Hopes
item.description: Oil prices moved lower after Japan’s Kyodo News Agency reported that Iran proposed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. lifts its blockade.

item.title: Here’s What Trump’s Greenland Deal Means for the U.S.
item.description: The agreement will clear the way for an expanded U.S. military presence on the Arctic island.

item.description: The president used the gathering of world leaders to deliver a campaign-style speech, declaring a “Golden Age of America.”

item.title: Trump Summit With Xi Unlikely to Include Chinese CEOs
item.description: The likely absence of a Chinese corporate delegation highlights the low expectations for significant business results from the meeting.

item.title: What Is Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline and Why Is It Rocking Oil Markets?
item.description: The pipeline, which was knocked out by attacks earlier this month, is now being tested and could resume flows within days.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Spent Months Trying to Bypass Hormuz. For Now, There’s No Way Around It.
item.description: With its Red Sea bypass route disrupted by attacks from Yemen and Iraq, the world’s oil kingpin is returning to the waterway it was trying to avoid in the first place.
